note: What each database actually holds for the parishes this archive needs. Checked before searching, every time — because a search of a source that does not cover your parish returns nothing, and nothing looks exactly like a negative result.

rows.note: Countess of Huntingdon's Chapel, Methodist Bishopston, Moravian Maudlin Street, Temple of Holy Cross. St Paul — the parish this archive needs — is not among them.
Stops 128 years before Hannah Saniger was born. Her baptism is untranscribed, not missing.
Covers the whole Saniger chain. This is where the chain was tested and failed.
With Dursley, holds 340 of the 494 Saniger records in the county.
Tested as the alternative reading of the tree's “Berkley”. The family there is SINGER throughout and holds no Hannah near 1805.

rows.holds: one D'Arcy record in the whole county
rows.note: That one record is Joseph D'Arcy's baptism, 19 March 1780, naming Robert and Jean. The 1779 marriage itself is not in the transcription.
Holds both the 1742 baptism that killed the Keele graft and the 1744 burial that may undo it.

128 Murdoch records exist for Ayrshire — Galston, Tarbolton, Ayr, Kirkoswald, Loudoun, Dailly, Beith, Dunlop — and not one for St Quivox. The county itself is thin: 202 Smiths for the whole eighteenth century.
Midlothian's holding is Edinburgh, Canongate, Restalrig and Dalry. Jean Ward's birth parish is not transcribed.
Zero records for the entire county. A control search for SMITH across the eighteenth century returns nothing. The county is offered in the search form and has no data behind it.
HO107/374 — this is where James and Hannah Wakefield were found, with Miriam aged one.

rows.holds: 221 Gloucestershire Wakefields, 31 in Bristol — but not this family
rows.note: Nationally only 36% of the 1851 pieces are transcribed. The piece covering Drivers Fields is not among them — which is why the Lyddya Sinegar identification is still an inference.
Control-tested at 21,248 Wakefield marriages for 1838–1842 before any absence was reported from it. This is where Miriam's birth registration was found.

rows.where: Prerogative Court of Canterbury wills, England
rows.holds: a wills index 1750–1800 and an administrations index 1660–1700
rows.note: NOTHING AFTER 1800. Three wills this archive needs — Robert D'Arcy's of 1827, Joseph D'Arcy's of 1848 and John Maddock Jones's of 1844 — are all beyond it. A paid trial does not help; the records are not there to unlock.

rows.where: Gloucestershire probate, Consistory Court of Gloucester
rows.note: Covers Berkeley and the whole Vale in the right years. Searched under wildcards for every form of the Saniger name and returns two entries, neither of them at Berkeley. A real negative, control-tested at 277 Smiths.

rows.where: Ireland Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage Licence Bonds, DUBLIN diocese
rows.note: Sorted by year, the latest Dublin-diocese entries in the entire set are a single 1813, a single 1752, and then a wall of 1741. The catalogue date range is the set's range, not the diocese's. An 1819 Wicklow marriage cannot be in it.

rows.where: Betham Prerogative Marriage Licences Abstracts, Ireland
rows.note: Ends nine years before the marriage this archive wants. Twenty-two Darcy entries, all necessarily too early.

rows.where: British consular and overseas registers (deaths abroad)
rows.note: Searched the whole record-set catalogue for “consular” and for “abroad” and both return no record sets at all. The Le Havre deaths of 1843 are not reachable here; they are on Ancestry and at Kew in RG 35.

rows.where: Caribbean Birth & Baptism Index — St Michael, Barbados
rows.note: Holds the two christenings of Robert D'Arcy's children at St Michael in 1786 and 1788. Barbados Births & Baptisms 1637-1891, a separate and larger set, holds neither — two indexes of the same island disagreeing about what is in them, which is its own warning.

The index is searchable on a paid trial and the transcripts are not — “Subscribe to unlock exclusive records”. Joseph D'Arcy's whole artillery career and a Constantine D'Arcy entry of 1777-79 are visible as dates and unreadable as records.
